column3: Ambient declarations for the slice of the Workers runtime the workerd lane uses; explains that full Workers types would conflict with Node's, and types the Durable Object storage as SQLite plus a synchronous kv.

Runs the shared storage-conformance suite against SQLite inside a Durable Object with a per-case table prefix, plus a version-1 -> version-2 schema migration that keeps its tasks and its exact index set.

The workerd vitest project: the cloudflareTest plugin with wrangler.jsonc, root set to test-workers/, include *.test.ts, and source-condition aliases for the package root, /testing and the sqlite/cloudflare subpath.

Three serverless-host behaviours: a task that sleeps through an eviction and resumes from its alarm, a turn cut off mid-stream recovered through the heartbeat alarm with the same requestId, and an object that can be evicted despite holding idle documents.
The reference host: a Durable Object that opens a Harness, arms an alarm before resume, keeps its faux script in KV so it survives eviction, and moves the Harness clock with a persisted offset.
Ten-line wrangler config: the SESSIONS Durable Object binding, nodejs_compat, and a new_sqlite_classes migration tag for the SQLite-backed object.
The chat fixture: a faux provider, a registry, live settings and reports; openChat, allEntries (oldest first), textOf, waitFor, unanswered (a response that never answers) and toolsNamed.
Measures code-mode overhead against a plain tool doing the same nested calls, sequentially and in parallel, reporting wall time and commits per call on SQLite.

Pins the built-in code-mode document checkpoint policies: task-scoped documents stay deltas until their task retires, and the codemode store takes a base after 64 deltas without changing historical reads or forks.

Pins the code-mode prompt surface: a constant tool description, the section's namespace-grouped catalogue, the token budget with every namespace represented first, deferred tools found by searchTools, and the grammar-constrained tool declaration.

Pins the models.* namespace: no credentials or headers in the catalog a script sees, classify and generateImages as hidden internal tools with their own usage, shape checks before the request, a four-call concurrency cap, and a note for images the script never showed.

The durable code-mode tool: journal-then-deliver, replay after a restart, divergence detection (a different call count, different arguments, a different end point) ending the call, the sandbox fingerprint guard, timeout across a restart, and the deterministic clock and randomness.
Compares appending to one array document with writing one family member per item, showing the array's per-append copy cost against the family's flat cost.

Property test over 5000 seeded random files: the streaming decoder equals decoding the whole input for any chunking (including a U+FEFF after an invalid sequence) and the line scanner agrees with decoding and splitting the whole file.
Runs the shared environment conformance suite against NodeExecutionEnv with native and polling watchers, plus the watch directory budget, a multi-chunk binary read and a FIFO refusal.

Mocks node:fs to make the spill stream slow and backpressured, then pins that inherited stdio stays open past the post-exit grace period so a descendant's delayed output is not lost, with the spill file byte-exact.

The Node environment's filesystem, line reader and shell: read/write/list/remove, symlinks, truncation, temp files, aborts, a strict-LF line reader, shell env overrides, timeouts, spawn errors and the spill thresholds.

Pins truncateHead and formatSize, including a child process with Buffer deleted to prove the byte counting does not depend on Node's Buffer, and the difference between a line-limit and a byte-limit truncation.
Runnable example: a Session over MemoryStorage, the BACKGROUND_CONTEXT cancellation contract, and one commit that creates an ownerless conversation.
Runnable example: a rewindable conversation document, the editable copy returned by tx.doc, and snapshot versus snapshotAsOf.
Runnable example: forking at an entry, the fork seeing only the parent's transcript up to that point, the document's own fork policy, and the fork's independence.
Runnable example: a background supervisor task owning a child conversation and a registry document, all created in one commit, with a fixed requestId for crash-safe delivery.
Runnable example: exposing a document as a live Chord state that never creates an absent document and delivers kind, sequence and value.
Runnable example: a document watch from one acquisition revision, serialised callbacks, and a full-value reset after 100 pending frames.
Runnable example: opening a Harness with a registry of extensions, the root conversation's id 1 created with its agent and init in one commit, and resolving the agent against the registry.
Runnable example: per-conversation agent choices stored by name, Harness-wide settings read live through getters, null clearing a field, and an uninstalled extension whose selection survives.
Runnable example: stateless conversation handles, typed entries, created conversations and a fork that inherits the parent's agent as of the fork entry.
Runnable example: the transcript-to-context derivation in one program, with an out-of-order tool result, an aborted answer, an edit and a summary head.
Runnable example: reloading an extension in place in one publication, wrapping a tool by name so the wrap survives a reload, and uninstalling by name.
Runnable example: an extension keeping its own per-conversation document, written by a tool and rendered by a section that treats a missing document as empty.

Runnable example: a two-phase durable task following intent, effect and outcome, with a memo-keyed idempotent payment, an abort handler that decides the outcome, and nothing running until resume or a wait.
Runnable example: close, reopen and continue, with a memo written before the effect so a rerun does not print the tick twice and a sleep stored with the checkpoint.
Runnable example: one chat turn with a faux model, submit returning a Submission, and the transcript holding the user input, the system prompt and the answer.
Runnable example: system-prompt sections, a section wrapper, per-conversation instructions rendered last, the environment's cwd, and only the change appended when the cwd changes.
Runnable example: a real OpenAI stream watched through the live document, printing only the new suffix of each committed partial, with the final answer read from the entry.
Runnable example: a coding-agent turn on JSONL storage with a hook timing a huge cat, each tool call running as a durable tool task owned by the generation.
Runnable example: print mode, one prompt and one answer, with the host awaiting its own Submission and a non-zero exit code on an unanswered input.
Runnable example: JSON mode in two vocabularies (agent events and raw view ops), the watch attached before the submit, and the storage location printed to stderr.
Runnable example: what happens to inputs, steers, writes, a rejection and a withdrawal while the conversation is busy, and the order they are placed in.
Runnable example: a client attaching mid-run, through the view and through the event stream, reconstructing the tool output from trims and appends.
Runnable example: a subagent as a tool that owns a child conversation, is safe to rerun through the ownership record and the requestId, and whose events a UI attaches to through the parent's details.
Runnable example: persistent background subagents (spawn, send, stop, status) with an anchor task, a reporter task, unsafe replay for stop, and a report that still arrives after a restart.
Runnable example: a checkout task owning four payment tasks, waiting with failFast, each payment refunding its own effect on abort, and the live task graph printed as a tree.
Runnable example: a long chat against a 3000-token window, background and blocking thresholds, a manual compaction whose summary waits for the boundary, and a provider overflow compacted once.
Runnable example: the coding tools, a cwd-aware prompt, live settings through getters, and an environment that follows the conversation's directory without a restart.
Runnable example: a read-only plan mode entered and left by changing the conversation's agent selection, with the switch visible to the model as a system-prompt change.
Runnable example: a reviewer agent with a cheaper model, a read-only tool set, its own directory, and a review loop as an onYield hook.
Runnable example: one sandbox per conversation looked up from a per-conversation document, with a conversation without a sandbox getting no environment at all.
Runnable example: replacing bash for some conversations by selection, and a wrapper that decorates whichever bash wins because wrappers never capture a base tool.

Runnable example: an extension reloaded while a call runs (the running call finishes on the old code) and a restart where the stored selection is a name that binds to whatever the new process installs.
Two-line preload that deletes the Node Buffer global before the measured module graph, so a module can be observed in a browser-like runtime.
The child script the Buffer-less truncation test drives: it prints the byte lengths, a truncation result and whether Buffer was really absent, as one JSON line.

Tasks that cannot run: the restart limit and parking, a close counting no restart, a faulted abort handler, progress resetting the count, a failed migration and a missing definition, and the wake staying active through recovery.

Who may call a tool: callers model versus tools, modelTools narrowing the offer, tools disabling what modelTools cannot restore, an unoffered call answered as unavailable, and addTools applying to the model's offer.

The barrier between an abort request and the work it must reach: a phase may not advance before the cascade's mark commits, a failFast request overrides a restart mark, restart marks upgrade down the tree, and a held outcome survives an abort.

The whole compaction surface: cut selection by budget and pairing, serialisation without thinking, manual, background, blocking and overflow compaction, per-model overrides, the hook that declines, recovery across reopen, the event order and the inbox interaction.

The model context derivation: excluded stop reasons, head markers, edits, tool-result ordering and synthesis, the baseline-lead rule case by case, incremental extended reads, retention, and the deep freeze of the returned range.

Conversation lifecycle: the lazily created root, forks at an entry with the as-of agent, pagination, the agent document's whole-field replace and null clearing, the three ways a conversation gets its documents, and rejection after close.

The agent event stream: lifecycle events and text deltas, tool start and result entries, queued submissions and retries, the 100-batch snapshot replacement, the sliding output window, one exact batch per turn boundary, and the late joiner.
Queued inputs behind a failed run: the default keeps them queued, continue starts the next run, withdraw settles them unanswered with run_failed, and queued writes are placed or kept per policy.

Generation recovery: an interrupted prepare reruns, an interrupted request resends the pinned request and its old options, a committed partial becomes an aborted entry and is not resent, a retry backoff survives a reopen, a deferred poll resumes, and a vanished model fails as no_model.

The generation turn: the answer and its settlement, partials as deltas and a base when idle, no_model, the durable retry backoff, the retry policy disabled, a deferred response polled, abort converting the partial, request options forwarded, provider session ids kept request-local, and the partial throttle.

The host's live objects: models and settings may be functions, generation calls the models function per request, a tool sees the current models through the identity-marked view, and a settings change applies to the next turn.

The durable input queue: writes before user items, followUpMode all, the two boundaries, steers at postTools, a queued reset ending the run, stale head writes, withdrawal, survival across reopen, the inbox's base exactly when empty, and the usage ledger.
Inputs that carry their own entry kind (which may not start with pi.) and data-only writes that change nothing the model sees, are queued behind a reset, and leave a preparing request unchanged.

Harness.inspect(): every live task's derived state without running task code, the ready, running, waiting and blocked states, the missing_task, task_too_old and migration_failed reasons, a migration not run to find out, and the unsettled submissions.

Harness open and close: the original error rethrown, joining handlers that ignore their signal before closing Storage, no frame published from a commit settling during close, the seal rejecting later operations, a read-only viewer never scheduling, and the registry at resume.

The live document's delta shape: one field write per tool start, the sliding tail window as a trim plus an append, the whole-window fallback, leaf-by-leaf details, partial text as appends, a base exactly when nothing runs, and the aborted tool's field-level ops.

Nested calls across a restart: a replay-unsafe caller's calls abandoned, a replay-safe caller's calls recovered and reattached by key, a rerun that calls differently rejected, the owned work of an abandoned call abandoned, and background work left running.

Nested tool calls: one document per call keyed by its key, each call its own task and id, the hooks seeing their parent, a key usable only for an identical call, the caller aborting the calls it left running, the slots found by binary search, and the invalid keys rejected.

The ownership tree: a conversation held busy by its foreground subtree, cascades through ended tasks and across background, ownership queries off finished subtrees, deep chains, the abort of a conversation with its four different effects, the marks a crash left unapplied, and the invocation-bound handle.

The prompt planner: sections rendered with tags and wrappers and a failing section keeping its last text, the replayed sections, minimal value patches and removals, an order change rewritten as two entries, the post-head baseline, and the tool loadout's minimal adds, removes and order rewrite.

The registry: install replaces in place and keeps the position, uninstall by name, validation of duplicate tools, duplicate sections, a bad key, the reserved instructions key and a task-name collision, the built-in tasks that are not an extension, and agent resolution of extensions, tools, sections, wrappers and hooks.

The report channel: a task's error and fault naming the extension that installed its definition, a replaced extension still named, section, hook and environment failures typed apart, and the listener, onWake, setTimer and session_failed reports distinguished.

The scheduler's in-memory indexes: a cascade's reason taken from the nearest cancelling owner, a chain of held owners finalised in one commit, a scope busy after reopen for work below an unloaded chain, and ownedTasks listing, ordering and rejecting after the invocation ends.

What the scheduler forgets: ended chains dropped, chains reloaded for new work below them, a chain kept when one commit ends a task and creates work below it, a rejected commit's load dropped, a 20,000-deep chain forgotten without recursion, and no growth against a fresh reopen.

Sleeping tasks: a sleep without an invocation, across a reopen, the timer versus onWake, a due sleep run at any pass, the timer disarmed on abort and close, a sleep in an abort handler rejected, and a task without a definition not counting as active.

A failed storage call: the first error ends the call, later calls, waits, watches and running tasks; reads and commits fail differently; the backend closes only after a paged read; a StorageRequestError fails one call; a throwing listener fails the session; and a listener, watch or clock failure stays local.

The three views of one tool result: what the caller gets, what the transcript stores and what the model sees, with a schema tool's validated output kept out of the transcript, broken structured output becoming an error result, and an error's text never becoming structured output.

The task model: ownership, allSettled and failFast waits, the wait-for cycle rejected at three depths, the completing hold, bottom-up abort order, the boundaries, recovery, the tool round, one turn_end per generation, and a held outcome never migrated.

Submissions: an idle write settled without a turn, a busy input rejected with ConversationBusy writing nothing, request-id deduplication before the busy check, abort results, a cancelled wait, a submission reacquired after reopen, scheduling enabled by submitting or waiting, and settlement in the same commit.
The registry-level fixture: fake tools, message builders, a compact message renderer, and addTool, addTask, addHooks and addSection installers that each return an uninstaller.

The live task graph: the statuses, owner edges and owned conversations, surviving tasks as pending after reopen, conversations listed in id order whatever the commit order, a cancelled acquisition registering nothing, and no revision for a commit that changes no node.

Task recovery: an intent/effect/outcome task resumed across close and reopen, each abort crash point walked in turn, blocked tasks kept pending until a fitting definition appears, an aborted blocked task orphaned, definition handover at the phase boundary, and an abort mark that races a handover preserved.

The task engine: phases and checkpoints, a phase without durable progress faulting, a committed terminal outcome kept, memos until terminal, task documents retired, the runtime's ordered commits and post-invocation rejection, scheduling, abort and the close seal.
The type contract of HarnessOptions.telemetry: one adapter with optional propagation and metrics, the option optional, and a partial object a compile error.

The content-free telemetry: submit and phase spans with nested parents, checkpoints only on a phase change, a steer linked to the current run without moving its work, entry events only after a successful commit, reports as fixed-field events, and a resumed invocation marked.

The tool task's recovery: an unsafe tool answered with its durable partial, a rerun only when both policies are safe, the environment rebuilt from the cwd, beforeTool rerun before the intent, an aborted tool answered with its partial, and the interrupted attempt's progress cleared.

The tool round: the input, call, result and answer, calls to tools not offered, the execution mode read once per round, parallel versus sequential, the result's retained output and diagnostics, argument validation and repair, the beforeTool and afterTool chains, addTools, the generation hooks and the tool execution api.

The conversation view: the hydrated entries and documents, one frame per touching commit, shared unchanged parts, the cut at a head marker, a fork's inherited entries, retirement and recreation, the 100-frame replacement, independent states and watches, and a failing listener isolated.
A heap-snapshot helper for the memory benchmarks: it sums the self size of every node in a fresh snapshot, because heapUsed after a GC counts what the collector has not compacted yet.
Creates the image processor from a compiled WebAssembly module, as Cloudflare Workers pass it, in its own file so Photon is not yet initialised.

The IndexedDB backend: the shared conformance suite run twice, once with a storage that reopens after every commit, plus minted ids surviving a reopen, a failed document copy rolling back the table writes, fork-ancestry scans and one large mixed transaction.

The JSONL storage: publication before reclamation, sidecar ordering and removal, a candidate serialised before I/O, a failure matrix per mode and per call, base and retirement reclamation, torn UTF-8 tails truncated at an exact offset, and the malformed and non-increasing records refused.
The in-memory backend: the shared conformance suite, and that a prepared commit does not expose retained state and that applying it twice yields the same sequence.
Measures the storage cost of nested calls carrying images, comparing inline base64 in the arguments with a task-id reference resolved from the caller's NestedCallDoc, across both backends.
Measures the commits, bytes by write type, stored size and heap of nested calls, streaming and nested at two depths, with and without progress, and asserts the tool results really succeeded.
Live regression for the provider-side prompt cache: the same durable session id forwarded on every turn, a first-turn cache miss and three later turns at a cache-read share of at least 0.9.
Measures the scheduler's fan-out cost with one tool making N parallel nested calls on memory storage, and fails the run whose nested calls failed.

Measures the scheduler's ownership index sizes and retained heap over many subagent cycles, and fails when the indexes grow with ended history; also prices a later message into an old subagent conversation.

The checkpoint and migration machinery: the predicate's receiver, the delta count passed to it, the predicate skipped for an empty batch but called for a structural no-op, a throwing predicate rolling back every prepared document, migration once per cold load, and a rejected migration leaving the session usable.

The type contract of document and entry definitions: an explicit checkpoint predicate required, a positive integer version, every scoped owner, key and seed overload typed, and the historical reads, states and watches restricted per scope.

Measures the document cache across many conversations at four retention settings, after a warm-up, reporting the cached count, the retained bytes per conversation and the cost of re-reading an old document.

The eviction rules: an unattached document evicted once its retention passed, a watched one never, a tracker held by a transaction never taken, history and forks kept after eviction, a family bounded, a retention that is not milliseconds treated as the default, Infinity as never, and one sweep job for the whole session.

The document transaction model: the initial base adopted after the storage succeeds, shared immutable snapshots, pointer-swap adoption, empty batches suppressed, escaped drafts revoked, every change aborted on a failed callback, retirement and recreation, and a token whose semantics disagree refused.

How a fork copies documents: as-of and current bases copied while initial documents stay absent, the entry-owning ancestor chosen, the stored value copied without consulting migrations, an invisible fork point refused, a rollback on assembly failure, and only conversation documents copied.

The Chord-backed document state: an absent document never created, contiguous deliveries, independent states, the exact committed value shared, a late baseline, retirement publishing null, a cold-loaded fork copy, a migrated tracker hydrated without writing, and unfrozen shared values.
The Session fixture: a MemoryStorage that can hold, crash and fail a commit at exact points, plus the open-test-session helper, the publication helpers and flush.

The table API: reads only before the first table write, caller-selected limits and cursors, minted ids, a staged task owner, missing and terminal owners rejected atomically, table JSON taken over, a task and its document in one transaction, and task documents retired at terminal settlement.

The document watch: the acquisition revision held until start, serialised callbacks with exact frames buffered, 101 pending commits collapsed to one root replacement, the in-flight frame never folded, retirement delivered, close stopping delivery, and a listener failure settling only its watch.
A vitest setup file that lets the whole suite run with documents evicted right after use, through the PI_DURABLE_DOCUMENT_RETENTION_MS environment variable.
The spec's usage examples, compile-checked with the application-supplied names declared, and the same patterns also run end to end under test/examples.

The Durable Object SQLite adapter: the conformance suite, the unprefixed default schema, pi's tables prefixed without touching the host's, two prefixes isolated on one object, and invalid or reserved prefixes refused.

The portable SQLite facade: the chord drivers re-exported without wrapping, each statement prepared once per connection, commits read in call order, admitted reads finishing before close, ids adopted only after settlement, and a document read racing a base replacement.

The SQLite migrations: the current schema applied repeatedly, a version 1 database migrated to admit sleeping tasks with its rows and indexes, a newer database refused, and a failed migration rolled back with the stored data kept for a retry.

The SQLite storage: records, sequences and ids surviving a reopen, prefixed tables, an invalid prefix and corrupted metadata refused, a document without its base refused, the WAL checkpointed and truncated, current-only revisions reclaimed, and the right indexes used for each query.

Measures the memory and disk footprint of the three backends, one child process per backend and scale with --expose-gc, reporting heap, RSS and the disk footprint including SQLite pages and JSONL file counts.
Pins the portable/runtime boundary by walking each public entry's import graph: the package root, the sqlite, env and jsonl subpaths must not reach a Node implementation.

The vitest benchmark lane for the three backends: every scenario validated against its expected result before it is timed, a pool of pre-seeded fixtures for the write benchmarks, and a copied storage per sample for the reopen benchmark.

Live regression for the prompt cache when a tool is added mid-conversation: the cache-read share is below 0.2 with the system message moved back and above 0.8 with it leading, measured against the real Anthropic stream.
The task fixture: deferred promises, an abort-aware wait, a poll-until helper, openTasks with a registry of tasks and collected reports, and a registry reader that counts live subscriptions.

Measures the tool-output path: the throttle, the live commits and their op bytes, the whole-string sets, the storage commit latency percentiles, a mid-round close and the replay on reopen, and the 1 GiB firehose.

The deferred-tool mechanism: tool_search appending a declaration so the cached prefix holds, loads recorded by name with remove winning, a loaded tool surviving a missing extension, per-branch loads, and a search that finds nothing loading nothing.

Reading images: the size and format limits, a refused image read without reading it, an image that changes while read being read again, the Photon processor's scaling and re-encoding, EXIF orientation in JPEG and WebP, the header-based dimensions, a Buffer-free base64 and the worker-thread implementation.

The differential test of the bounded read tool against the kept whole-file reference, over 400 random files and 4 random offset/limit pairs including NaN, negatives and fractional values, with the output and diagnostics matching exactly.

The built-in tools: read with offsets, limits, truncation and a growing log, write and the per-path mutation queue, edit's disjoint matching and overlap rejection, the JSON-shape repairs, BOM and CRLF preservation, PowerShell and bash, and the command prefix.

The type contract of the public types: branded ids by record kind, a TaskId carrying its result type, the discriminated unions of task state, submissions and document content, and the erased-into-an-extension task.

The package build config: the sibling packages resolved to their built declarations, src as the only input, and the photon-wasm ambient declaration added through files because exclude drops every d.ts.
The benchmark lane: only test/**/*.bench.ts, verbose reporting and the source condition, with no aliases because the benchmark files import the sources relatively.
The package's test configuration: the source condition and two aliases so tests run against src rather than a stale dist, the workerd lane excluded, and the document-retention setup file.

Builds the code-mode prompt surface: a fixed tool description and a codemode system section listing the callable tools as TypeScript declarations, grouped by namespace and fitted to a token budget, with every namespace represented before any is complete.
Boilerplate barrel: re-exports the code-mode extension and tool factories, the store document, the reserved names and the namespace type, and publishes CODEMODE_MODULE_VERSION.

The models.* globals for code-mode scripts: catalog lookups plus classify and generateImages as internal tools with callers ["tools"], so paid effects get their own durable task, live row, abort and usage accounting; models are resolved by provider and id only.

Formats a code-mode script's result for the model: a header with the wall time, per-item markers, one console_output block, images written to temp files, and a token-budget truncation that keeps the head and the tail and spills the complete text.

Defines the durable document model: defineDoc and defineDocFamily with a typed scope, history and fork semantics, a stable id derived from the logical address, and materialisation through the definition's migrate().
Declares the six transcript entry kinds with their is() guards; each entry's docstring states who writes it and what its model, head and data carry.
Byte-exact UTF-8 decoding helpers: a range decoder that turns off Node's streaming BOM handling and a StreamDecoder that strips a leading mark itself, so decoding in pieces equals decoding whole.

The portable ExecutionEnv contract: a Result return type instead of exceptions, FileError and ExecutionError with stable codes, a FileSystem and Shell covering reads, bounded positional reads, paging, listing, watching, and shell exec with spill and a caller-side tail window.
LineScanner: computes the byte ranges and decoded sizes of a line range of an arbitrarily large file from bytes fed in order, in bounded memory, with an exact first-line size.

NodeFileWatcher: watches by snapshot diff rather than trusting OS events, polls on Windows and on unreliable filesystems, hashes recently modified small files in polling mode, and re-reconciles a watcher when a directory's identity changes.

NodeExecutionEnv: the local ExecutionEnv - a strict-LF line reader, a bounded positional binary reader, a directory reader, shell discovery with Git Bash on Windows and a WSL stdin transport, process-tree kill, and a spill path with backpressure.

Four error types with distinct semantics: an error formatter that never throws, ReadAfterWrite for a table read after the first write, StorageRequestError that fails one read but not the Session, and SessionFailed and ConversationBusy.

Resolves the effective agent: composes extension tools, sections and wrappers, filters by the stored tools and modelTools with a deferred-tool loadout, and defines the default retry, compaction and progress policies and the settings merge.

The compaction task: selects a cut that never separates a tool call from its result, summarises the dropped prefix with a pinned prompt that omits thinking, and places the summary directly or through a write submission.

Derives the active transcript and model context from committed entries: bounds captured on the Session line, a previous range reused, the JSON frozen, tool results ordered after their assistant with a missing one synthesised, and the first system message led only when it is the baseline.

Identity and typing helpers for extension authors - defineExtension, defineTool, section, hook, wrapTool and wrapSection; the rules are that a section key matches a regex and is not the reserved instructions key, and that a hook binds to the task's name.
Translates each commit publication into an ordered batch of agent events by diffing the before and after pi.live view and decoding the Chord view ops into text, thinking and tool-call deltas.

The generation task - the harness's agent loop: prepare, request, classify (deferred poll, tool round, answer, overflow compaction, retry) and the tools phase, with every assistant entry written through appendAssistant so the usage stays complete.

Harness.open and the Conversation handle: root, fork and independent creation, submit, compact, reset, abort and waitForIdle, the rule that only the Harness writes model context to a busy conversation, the invocation-bound handle, and the failure containment.

The durable input queue: prepareBoundary and applyBoundary at the postTools and final boundaries under the steering and follow-up modes, and a write whose head points before the active range marked stale rather than applied.

assignJson: assigns a value leaf by leaf into an existing container so Chord records a string reassignment as an append instead of a whole-container set - the mechanism that keeps a streamed partial from being republished whole.

The pi.live document: run control, the current generation attempt, the tool round's slots, the nested call slots and the compaction statuses; the checkpoint rule makes a complete base whenever nothing runs.

Prompt planning: replaySections rebuilds the sections in effect, planSystemEntries computes the minimal pi.system patch that makes the replayed sections and tools equal the desired ones, and planTools keeps byte-equal declarations so the prefix stays cacheable.

The provider-facing conversation identity: pi.provider holds a uuidv7 session id, every fork starts with a fresh one, and a legacy conversation is migrated in one commit rather than on the request path.

The extension registry: an immutable published snapshot of installed extensions, their tools, sections and tasks, with duplicate tool names, duplicate section keys, the reserved instructions key and a built-in task name all refused.

The durable task scheduler: the task and conversation ownership tree, phases reserved and run on the Session line, waits validated against the wait-for graph, abort cascades derived from durable intent so a crash repairs them, a task parked at the restart limit, and wake() for the host.

Durable submissions: admitSubmission decides in one commit whether a draft is placed, queued, refused or stale, a display-only write bypasses the queue, a known requestId returns the existing submission, and a steer's span is linked to the running generation's trace.

The live task graph as a replicated Chord state: nodes with status, phase, owned conversations and a blocked reason, the reason re-derived when the registry changes so a task no definition can take shows as blocked without a commit.
The content-free telemetry vocabulary: two spans, three metrics and the event schemas - deliberately no error payloads, only ids and fixed enumerations.
